origin.description: Format strings and write them with cat.
origin.usage: stri_printf(format, ..., file = "", sep = "\n", append = FALSE, na_string = "NA", inf_string = "Inf", nan_string = "NaN", use_length = FALSE)

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: A character vector of format strings.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: A path or connection. The default writes to standard output.

arguments.name: append
arguments.text: If TRUE, append to an existing file.

arguments.name: na_string
arguments.text: Text used for a missing value. The default is the string NA.

origin.details: Formatting matches stri_sprintf. cat inserts sep between elements. When sep contains a newline, the output also ends with a newline.
origin.example: path <- tempfile(); stri_printf("%s", c("a", "b"), file = path); cat(paste0("stri_printf(\"%s\", c(\"a\", \"b\")) writes ", paste(as.integer(readBin(path, "raw", 20)), collapse = ", "), ".\n"))

translation.description: Format strings and write them with cat.
translation.usage: stri_printf(format, *args, file='', sep='\n', append=False, na_string='NA', inf_string='Inf', nan_string='NaN', use_length=False)

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: A format string, or a list of them.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: A path. The default writes to standard output.

arguments.name: append
arguments.text: If True, append to an existing file.

arguments.name: na_string
arguments.text: Text used for a missing value. The default is the string NA.

translation.details: Formatting matches stri_sprintf. When sep contains a newline, the written text also ends with a newline, including for an empty result. A path is encoded as UTF-8. The return value is None.
translation.example:
import tempfile
path = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False).name
stri_printf("%s", ["a", "b"], file=path)
bytes = ", ".join(str(item) for item in Path(path).read_bytes())
print(f"stri_printf('%s', ['a', 'b']) writes {bytes}.")
